exact_statement: For a fixed finite connected undirected graph G=(V,E), disjoint nonempty A,B, state energies E_x, symmetric fixed prefactors a_e>0, and edge transition levels S_e, define μ_β(x)=exp(-βE_x), q_β(x,y)=a_e exp(-β(S_e-E_x)), and γ(S)=min over A-to-B paths of max edge S_e. The chain is reversible with conductance c_β(e)=a_e exp(-βS_e), and lim_{β→∞} -β^{-1}log cap_β(A,B)=γ(S). With E_A=min_{x∈A}E_x, lim_{β→∞}-β^{-1}log(cap_β(A,B)/μ_β(A))=γ(S)-E_A.
assumptions: fixed finite connected graph as β tends to infinity
positive symmetric edge prefactors independent of β
Arrhenius transition rates with a shared edge transition level in both directions
capacity defined by the reversible Dirichlet principle
novelty_boundary: Cirillo-Nardi-Sohier's general rare-transition communication-height and escape-exponent theory already includes transition costs. The present path/cut proof is an explicit reversible Arrhenius specialization; no priority claim is made.

costs.input: Full finite graph, state energies, and edge transition levels or conductances are required.
costs.compute: Bottleneck-path exponent can be computed by threshold connectivity in O(|E| log |E|); many-body state graph size can be exponential.
costs.physical_energy: No lab work, material sample energy, or compute joules were measured.

falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the finite reversible Arrhenius assumptions with a capacity exponent different from the minimum bottleneck edge level would falsify the theorem; the proof's path/cut bounds rule this out under its assumptions.
next_gate: Validate that a measured or simulated nucleation model has a fixed finite reversible Arrhenius graph and independently acquired transition levels.

exact_statement: On the three-state path 0-1-2 with energies (0,1,-1), unit edge prefactors, and A={0}, B={2}, edge levels (1,1) and (1,1+δ) yield identical Gibbs families, state-energy landscapes, state saddle, and transition topology but escape exponents 1 and 1+δ. Any exponent prediction based only on the shared static input has worst-case absolute error at least δ/2. Since δ can be arbitrarily large absent a kinetic bound, static data have no finite uniform exponent-error guarantee.
assumptions: same finite state graph and state energies for both models
detailed-balance Arrhenius edge rates as defined in PN-C2-01
δ>0 is not bounded by the supplied static information
novelty_boundary: The general fact that transition costs affect metastability is established prior art. This is an elementary sharp minimax witness isolating non-identifiability from Gibbs weights and state saddles; it is not claimed as a novel metastability theorem.

costs.input_missing: A static-only estimator omits edge transition levels or equivalent kinetic conductances.
costs.data: No physical data required for the mathematical counterexample.

falsifier: The exact mean hitting-time formula for this three-state chain or a Gibbs/state-saddle-only estimator with a uniform finite error bound over all δ would contradict the claim.
next_gate: Measure edge hazards or supply a justified finite interval for kinetic barriers; otherwise report the exponent as unidentifiable.

exact_statement: For a finite reversible CTMC with known state masses μ and correct graph, if directed edge counts N_e over fixed cumulative occupation exposure t_e are Poisson(t_e q_e), exact Garwood intervals with Bonferroni allocation α/|E| give simultaneous edge-rate coverage at least 1-α. Mapping to conductance intervals and using monotonicity of Dirichlet capacity yields a 1-α interval [cap(c^-)/μ(A), cap(c^+)/μ(A)] for the finite-temperature capacity-normalized rate. If known Arrhenius prefactors permit transforming rate intervals into edge-level intervals, the minimum-bottleneck-path functional yields a simultaneous confidence interval for the asymptotic exponent.
assumptions: finite reversible CTMC with correctly enumerated transition graph
known equilibrium masses μ for the finite-temperature rate interval
known cumulative occupation exposure in each source state and correctly labeled directed transitions
known edge prefactors are additionally required for single-temperature asymptotic barrier transformation
novelty_boundary: Garwood intervals, Bonferroni coverage, and capacity monotonicity are standard ingredients. Their composition into this stated graph-rate interface is a conditional construction; novelty and priority have not been searched exhaustively or established.

costs.data: Requires state-labeled transition counts and occupation exposures on relevant edges; rare-event exposure scales as 1/q_e and can grow exponentially with β times the edge barrier.
costs.equilibrium: Known μ(A) or aggregated state masses may require exhaustive enumeration or umbrella sampling; that acquisition cost is not included in the edge-count interval.
costs.compute: Two finite weighted-Laplacian Dirichlet solves; dense worst-case O(|V|^3), sparse methods depend on graph conditioning.
costs.energy: No lab or compute joules measured.

falsifier: Under valid fixed-exposure CTMC sampling, repeated coverage trials below nominal coverage or a held-out rate outside its interval beyond sampling coverage would falsify at least one count, graph, reversibility, mass, or interval-propagation assumption.
next_gate: Implement the interval calculation on a specified graph and compare predictions against independent held-out first-passage or forward-flux samples.

exact_statement: For a preregistered nucleation coarse state z=(n,j), where n is largest stable-phase cluster size and j a candidate nucleation location, edge-hazard capacity estimation gives an exact reduced-chain rate interval only if the projection is Markov-sufficient (strong lumpability suffices) and reversible. Committor concentration and lag-transition checks are necessary falsification gates for this proposed reduction; failure requires more coordinates or the microscopic state graph.
assumptions: finite measured (n,j) state graph and correct event labeling
strong lumpability or another proof of Markov sufficiency
reversible aggregated generator and known aggregated equilibrium masses
novelty_boundary: Yao-Jack's RFIM simulations already motivate location-augmented reaction coordinates and show residual shape-fluctuation deviations. This graph-capacity estimator is a conditional proposed interface; no claim of general physical adequacy or methodological priority is made.

costs.data: Requires repeated metastable trajectories, event labels, cumulative occupation times, saved configurations for committor shooting, and lag tests.
costs.compute: Capacity solves scale with coarse graph size; if lumpability fails, expanding to shape/microstates can be exponential.
costs.sample_energy: Reset, imaging, and apparatus costs are system-specific and unmeasured.

falsifier: Broad committor distributions conditional on (n,j), non-exponential dwell times, lag-dependent transition probabilities, or held-out rates outside the predicted interval falsify the two-coordinate model or another named assumption.
next_gate: Select a named disordered nucleation model, preregister zones and thresholds, run committor/lag admission tests, and compare held-out capacity predictions with forward-flux rates.

exact_statement: The finite reversible Arrhenius graph theorem and conditional (n,j) estimator do not establish transition barriers, reversibility, Markov sufficiency, local equilibration, or an escape rate for any real material without system-specific measurement and validation.
assumptions: no named material or measured transition-rate dataset supplied
novelty_boundary: No physical-material claim or design recommendation is made; primary sources concern mathematical models and simulation evidence.

costs.data: Requires material-specific order parameter, state/transition graph or justified reduced coordinates, equilibrium weights, hazards, and repeated switching events.
costs.compute: Material-specific state identification and rare-event sampling must be separately charged.
costs.energy: No physical work or compute energy is known.

falsifier: A named material's calibrated measurements could establish a narrower transfer; absent such data, the transfer remains unknown.
next_gate: Acquire material-specific observations and independently validate the kinetic graph before making a physical rate prediction.
